definitions.gloss: to enter someone's house; to go inside; to walk right in
definitions.explanation: To step up into someone's home and make oneself comfortable. Often implies entering without much hesitation or formality, sometimes with a nuance of presumptuousness.

examples.english: Walk right into a friend's house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{勝手|かって}に→勝手に：32383_katteni⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{上|あ}がり{込|こ}んで⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧いけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't just walk into someone's house without permission.

examples.japanese: ⟦{近所|きんじょ}→近所：01318_kinjo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{上|あ}がり{込|こ}んできて⟦{居間|いま}→居間：01745_ima⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んでいる→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: The neighborhood kids have come barging in and are playing in the living room.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of ⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧ (to step up into a house) and ⟦{込|こ}む→込む：00719_komu⟧ (fully inside). Japanese homes have a raised floor above the entrance, so entering literally means stepping up; ⟦{込|こ}む→込む：00719_komu⟧ adds going right in and settling. It ranges from neutral (friends dropping in) to slightly negative (barging in uninvited).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{上|あ}がり{込|こ}む (to enter someone's house)
- ⟦{勝手|かって}に→勝手に：32383_katteni⟧{上|あ}がり{込|こ}む (to enter without permission)
- {上|あ}がり{込|こ}んで⟦{居座|いすわ}る→居座る：15930_isuwaru⟧ (to come in and stay on)

WRITING:
Also written {上|あ}がりこむ.
